name: Leadpages
tagline: Build conversion-focused landing pages and connect form submissions to email

tiers.name: HTML Pub Starter
tiers.limits: 5 published pages; 1 custom domain; 1 GB storage; 4,000 AI credits/month
tiers.notes: The main pricing cards were showing a $5 introductory amount; a separate official pricing page states the recurring price is $10/month. Annual equivalent applies the stated 20% annual discount.

tiers.name: HTML Pub Pro
tiers.limits: 25 pages; 1 custom domain; 5 GB storage; 1 blog; 90-day analytics; 12,000 AI credits/month
tiers.notes: The main pricing cards were showing $15; the separate official HTML Pub pricing page states $29/month recurring.

tiers.name: HTML Pub Business
tiers.limits: 50 pages; 2 custom domains; 10 GB storage; 2 blogs; deeper analytics and lead export; 20,000 AI credits/month
tiers.notes: The main pricing cards were showing $25; the separate official HTML Pub pricing page states $49/month recurring.

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: Unlimited traffic/pages; 4 domains/sites; 3 blogs; 15 GB storage; 2 A/B variants; 2,000 IP and 1,000 lead enrichments/month; 40,000 AI credits
tiers.notes: Limited introductory first month is advertised around $49-$50; recurring monthly price is $99 and annual equivalent is $79.

tiers.name: Optimize
tiers.limits: Unlimited traffic/pages; 6 domains/sites; 5 blogs; 25 GB storage; 4 A/B variants; 5,000 IP and 2,500 lead enrichments/month; 80,000 AI credits; 3 team seats
tiers.notes: Limited introductory first month is advertised around $99-$100; recurring monthly price is $199 and annual equivalent is $159.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited traffic/pages; 10 domains/sites/blogs; 50 GB storage; 10,000 IP and 5,000 lead enrichments/month; 160,000 AI credits; 10 team seats and workspaces
tiers.notes: Main card was showing $200 during the launch promotion; recurring price is $399 and annual equivalent is $319.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no live-publishing free tier; pages can be built and previewed free in HTML Pub, but publishing requires a paid plan; 7-day paid-plan trial requires a card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (20% off, billed once yearly); limited first-month discounts are separate from recurring prices
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI credit top-up packs start at $2.50; pages remain live only while subscribed on HTML Pub, and the low introductory figures shown on the main cards are not the ongoing recurring charges.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Leadpages, build conversion-focused landing pages and connect form submissions to email. The hard boundary is hosting, templates, experiments, integrations, and lead-delivery reliability, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble responsive sections into conversion-focused landing pages, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, connect form submissions to email, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: hosting, templates, experiments, integrations, and lead-delivery reliability
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Leadpages because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Webstudio

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Leadpages in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble responsive sections into conversion-focused landing pages, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, connect form submissions to email, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
